messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: Canary metrics for feature flag ff:ex_prompt_router_v2 breached thresholds (latency p95 2.4s -> 3.9s, 5xx rate +3.6%, and small sample of completions show hallucination patterns). Auto-canary paused. Paging oncall @nathan :rotating_light:

nathan: seeing the pager, joining. any customer impact numbers?

emily: several CS tickets from a handful of trial customers reporting garbage completions and timeouts, low volume but high severity for those accounts.

maya: logs show a spike in model timeouts and also an unexpected prompt rewrite happening in the new route. looks like rewrite middleware applied an extra template for some prompts.

alex: that middleware change was introduced in the v2 router to normalize prompts. it was gated but the canary user bucket got the new path. i'm running a query to compare before/after examples.

nathan: @alex can you pull the exact flag id and how to flip it? i want to cut traffic immediately if we confirm.

alex: flag id is ff:ex_prompt_router_v2. control plane exposes /api/flags/{id}/state. i can flip to OFF. quick curl: ```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://flags.internal.redwood/api/flags/ff:ex_prompt_router_v2/state \
  -d '{"state":"off","actor":"oncall","reason":"emergency canary kill"}'
```

nathan: proceeding to flip. will post result.

srebot: NOTE: oncall activity detected. Please add short notes with why toggle was done.

nathan: ran the curl, got 200. response: `\{"id\":\"ff:ex_prompt_router_v2\",\"state\":\"off\",\"updated_by\":\"nathan\",\"timestamp\":\"2026-03-15T17:14:12Z\"\}`

deploy-bot: Feature flag ff:ex_prompt_router_v2 set to OFF by nathan. Routing reverted to stable path for all traffic buckets.

jon: confirming traffic shift in router metrics — new-route for canary dropped from ~12% -> 0.1% within 30s.

maya: latency back to baseline p95 ~1.1s after ~45s. errors dropping. i'm tailing completions; early samples look normal.

emily: emailed affected customers with a short note: "we detected anomalous completions from an experimental route and disabled it; your history and data are unaffected. reach out for follow-up."

opslead: good call. who owns the root cause triage? carla? alex?

carla: i'll lead triage with alex and maya. immediate next steps: capture failing examples, preserve canary logs, open a SEV ticket and create a retrospective.

nathan: creating incident ticket now: INC-20260315-003 - Experimental prompt router canary generated hallucinations and latency; feature flag kill engaged. linking logs and screenshots.

srebot: Pager burn: 1 minute active, 18 pages suppressed. No escalation required.

alex: initial diff: middleware template added a fallback prompt fragment that duplicated context which appears to produce prompt misconditioning with some user inputs. unit tests missed because they used canonical prompts.

maya: saving failing request/response pairs to s3://incidents/1923456789/canary-samples.jsonl and snapshotting the canary container images.

jon: I ran a quick canary smoke locally against the stable and v2 router; v2 reproducibly returns malformed structured output for a subset of prompts (edge-case: nested JSON in user input).

carla: action items: (1) hold on release of v2 until safety filter + templating logic reexamined; (2) add canary gating for structured-prompt edgecases; (3) add automated smoke tests with nested-json inputs; (4) blameless postmortem.

opslead: add rollout rollback in release playbook: ensure ff kill path tested in staging, and add runbook snippet for immediate curl toggle.

nathan: handoff to day oncall @maya in 20 min. will post a short summary in the incident ticket and Slack.

nathan: summary: toggled ff:ex_prompt_router_v2 OFF at 17:14:12Z after canary breach. Mitigation validated ~17:15Z. No broad customer outage detected; small number of trial customers impacted. incident ticket created.

maya: acknowledged. i'll continue log analysis and run the new smoke-suite against more inputs. leaving a monitor on the flag and router error rate.

emily: following up with the customers who reported issues; will offer one-on-one calls if needed.

carla: timeline note: create a changelog entry in the release docs and postpone next canary until templating fix + tests in.

alex: prepping a PR to revert the micro-template and add new unit+smoke tests. will request review from maya and jon.

srebot: LOG: k8s event snapshot and router metrics archived to incident artifacts.

opslead: after-action: schedule 1hr triage at 18:00Z today to go through samples and decide go/no-go for reattempt. invite SRE, infra, product devex, and CS.

jon: quick note — we should add an automated canary comparator that checks outputs for hallucination heuristics (copy-to-copy differences, token-level surprises). filing a ticket.

nathan: handoff complete. leaving monitoring to maya. if anything spikes re-pager me. :thumbsup:

maya: will do. closing this Slack thread for active paging; continuing investigation updates will be posted in the incident ticket and a follow-up thread for postmortem notes.

deploy-bot: RESOLVED: Feature flag ff:ex_prompt_router_v2 rolled back to OFF and canary traffic reverted. Incident status: mitigated.

carla: thanks everyone — please add any further notes to INC-20260315-003. we want a blameless postmortem with remediation within 72 hours."
